# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-18
**Reference number:** POC-BDA4258628-91913
**Member:** Reese Foster
**Member ID:** W604114141
**Plan:** Blue Cross of Idaho (Commercial/ACA), State of Idaho
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Joint Surgery* — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/
**Appeal deadline:** This appeal must be received by 2027-02-14

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which Blue Cross of Idaho denied on 2026-08-18. The notice states, as the reason for the determination, that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records already in the prior authorization packet address the imaging criteria in the plan's own guidelines.

Below I set out the plan's published language and the matching entries in my records.

## 1. The type of imaging report the policy asks for

The plan's guidelines state:

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods: X-ray report or provider interpretation of x-rays that utilizes or can be correlated with the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system of osteoarthritis MRI report from a radiologist that utilizes or can be correlated with the modified Outerbridge or similar classification system related to articular cartilage injury and osteoarthritis"

My imaging is an MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-12 — well within the past 12 months of both the request and this appeal. It describes the degree of cartilage damage directly: full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment, and it is graded using the Kellgren-Lawrence system, at grade 4 medially. This is a graded report of cartilage loss, obtained inside the time window the policy names.

## 2. The severity of joint destruction the policy describes

The plan's guidelines state:

> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III – IV or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4, isolated to the medial or lateral knee compartment with no degenerative changes in the opposite compartment"

My MRI of 2026-07-12 documents Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially, which falls within the grade 3–4 range the plan itself identifies as significant joint destruction and cartilage loss. The findings reported are in the medial compartment: full-thickness cartilage loss with bone-on-bone apposition. If the plan's reviewer concluded that the opposite-compartment element of this criterion was not addressed, I ask that this be stated specifically so my surgeon can supply the compartment-by-compartment detail from the same study. [If the opposite (lateral) compartment is separately characterized in the 2026-07-12 MRI report, insert the radiologist's wording here.]

The plan's guidelines also state:

> "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis, or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

My report addresses one of the specific findings named in that sentence: bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment. [If the 2026-07-12 MRI report contains additional descriptive findings from this list, insert the radiologist's wording here.]

And the guidelines state:

> "For x-ray interpretation, the provider shall submit a detailed imaging description that correlates with clinical findings of the requested procedure. In the absence of a detailed description, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

My imaging findings line up with my clinical findings. On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. Functionally, I cannot climb stairs without assistance and I wake 3–4 times a night because of pain. Those are the everyday consequences of a knee with full-thickness medial cartilage loss and bone-on-bone apposition.

## 3. Symptom severity and function

The plan's guidelines state:

> "Reporting symptom severity – Severity of pain and its associated impact on activities of daily living (ADLs) and instrumental ADLs (IADLs) are key factors in determining the need for intervention. For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document 12 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest, an inability to climb stairs without assistance, and waking 3–4 times nightly from pain. [Insert the numeric pain score, out of 10, as recorded in the office notes.]

The guidelines also state:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

The packet contains all three of those elements: duration (12 months, progressive), specific functional limitations (stairs, sleep), and the type and duration of every treatment I tried, which I list next.

## 4. Conservative management

The plan's guidelines state:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

I completed both parts.

On physical therapy, the guidelines state:

> "Physical therapy requirement includes ANY of the following: Physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider of physical therapy services Supervised home treatment program that includes ALL the following: Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

I had supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-27, completing 20 visits. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

On the complementary strategy, the guidelines state:

> "Complementary conservative treatment requirement includes ANY of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Intra-articular corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

I met this more than once over: NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

On duration, the guidelines state:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"

My supervised physical therapy ran 8 weeks, and my NSAID trial ran 4 months. My imaging is graded Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially, which is the grade the plan names in its own parenthetical exception to the duration requirement. I ask the reviewer to apply that exception, or, if the plan reads the exception as limited to plain radiographs rather than the graded MRI in my file, to say so plainly so that my surgeon can respond.

On failure of that care, the guidelines state:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

My pain has been progressive over 12 months and is unrelieved by rest; the injection helped only partially and only for 4 weeks; the NSAIDs gave inadequate relief; and surgery is now being considered, which is the more invasive therapy the criterion refers to.

## 5. Reevaluation, knee stability, alignment, and comorbidities

The guidelines state:

> "Clinical reevaluation – In most cases, reevaluation should include a physical examination. Direct contact by other methods, such as telephone communication or electronic messaging, may substitute for in-person evaluation when circumstances preclude an office visit. Clinical reevaluation must be done in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service such that the patient’s condition would be unlikely to change by the date of service."

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. [Insert the date of the most recent in-person examination by Dr. Lindqvist, and the anticipated date of service.]

The guidelines state:

> "Intact anterior cruciate ligament or documentation of stable knee examination (UKA may done with concurrent ACL reconstruction if all other criteria are met)"

[Insert the examiner's documentation of ACL status or knee stability from the surgical consultation note.]

The guidelines state:

> "Less than 10 degrees of fixed varus deformity for medial UKA"

and

> "Less than 15 degrees of fixed valgus deformity for lateral UKA"

[Insert the measured fixed deformity in degrees, if recorded in the chart or on imaging.]

Finally, the guidelines state:

> "Where there are patient specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient, a shared decision-making process to discuss these modifiable comorbidities with the patient is strongly recommended and should be documented."

My records show no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## A note on what I was given

Several of the plan's criteria above are written as an introduction to a list of further conditions, and the full text of those lists was not provided to me. I am not going to guess at what they say. If the denial rests on any requirement not reproduced above, I ask that the plan identify, in writing, the specific criterion it applied and the specific record it found missing, so my surgeon and I can respond to the actual point in dispute.

## What I am asking for

I ask Blue Cross of Idaho to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-18 and authorize the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) requested by Dr. Lindqvist. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask for a written explanation identifying each criterion from the *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Joint Surgery* that the plan found unmet and the evidence the reviewer relied on, along with the reviewing clinician's name and specialty, and information about my next level of appeal, including external review.

This appeal must be received by 2027-02-14. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I may also call the number on my member ID card about this appeal.

Please contact me if any additional records would help. I will provide them promptly.

Thank you for your reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Reese Foster**
Member ID: W604114141
Reference number: POC-BDA4258628-91913
